title: RNA sequencing of human, IDH2-mutated, acute myeloid leukemia samples from patients before or during treatment with Enasidenib
description: Mutations in isocitrate dehydrogenase 2 (IDH2) occur in many cancers including Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML). Recently, we showed that single agent Enasidenib, a first-in-class, selective mutant IDH2 inhibitor, produces a 40% response in relapsed/refractory AML patients by promoting differentiation of leukaemic cells. In this current study, we describe two patients who responded to Enasidenib treatment but subsequently relapsed with an IDH2-mutant subclone which had acquired mutations in DHX15 and DDX1 genes.  These genes have putative functions in regulating splicing.  We have studied the alternative splicing events using RNASeq in the sample pre-relapse (before acquisition of DHX15 and DDX1 mutations) and at relapse (after acquisition of DHX15 and DDX1 mutations).

samples.title: Patient_201-013_preRelapse
samples.description: Protocols: Bone marrow samples were collected from patients at defined time points as part of a clinical trial protocol (AG-221-C-001) with informed consent. The focus of this study was on patients who had achieved complete remission in response to Enasidenib but subsequently relapsed. Bone marrow samples included in this dataset were collected before and after relapse. Patients were treated with Enasidenib according to clinical trial protocols of 100mg once daily of Enasidenib. Total RNA was extracted using Norgen RNA/DNA extraction kit. Copy DNA libraries constructed using Clontech SMARTer low input kit, followed by tagmentation and indexing using Illumina Nextera kit.
